criteria.statement: foreman_quality_baseline.py, token_bloat_diagnostic.py and security_privacy_convergence.py exist at the root of this repository, are tracked by git, and each one actually runs to completion and produces a parseable report.
criteria.verification: git -C /Users/m5/dev/dev-harness-run2 ls-files -- foreman_quality_baseline.py token_bloat_diagnostic.py security_privacy_convergence.py prints exactly those three paths and nothing else. Then each script is executed with /Users/m5/.venv/bin/python3 from a fresh empty directory and exits 0. Its JSON report must then satisfy content assertions a silently-broken analysis pass cannot produce, not merely parse as a non-empty object: foreman_quality_baseline reports files_analyzed >= 150 and functions_analyzed >= 900 (this tree holds 172 .py files before R23 adds three, measured 2026-09-02), and its hotspots array contains an entry for tessera/store/store.py with max_cc >= 30 and MI < 10 -- known-real values from the measured baseline, 32 and 4.78. security_privacy_convergence reports files_scanned >= 150 and at least 30 dependency pins actually queried. token_bloat_diagnostic reports session_files > 0 and a project_hint equal to the one passed on the command line. A script that exits 0 having analyzed nothing fails every one of these.

criteria.statement: Every report written by each of the three scripts carries tool_git_sha, tree_git_sha and formula_version, and the first two match the live repository state at the time of the run rather than a stored or placeholder value.
criteria.verification: Run each script, load its JSON report, and assert tool_git_sha, tree_git_sha and formula_version are present and non-empty. Assert report['tool_git_sha'] equals the independently computed output of git log -1 --format=%H -- <that script's path>, and report['tree_git_sha'] equals git rev-parse HEAD, both computed by the test itself and not read from the report. Then commit an unrelated change and re-run: tree_git_sha must differ from the previous run's value. formula_version must likewise be checked against live state, not merely for presence: assert the radon version it reports equals importlib.metadata.version('radon') as queried by the test itself (6.0.1 as installed 2026-09-02). A hardcoded literal such as 'radon-6.0.1' passes a presence check forever and goes on passing after a version bump, which defeats the entire reason the field exists -- making a dependency change that moves every number in a report visible without a tool SHA change or a tree diff. Presence and live-match are not sufficient on their own for formula_version, because the reported value can coincide with the installed one: a hardcoded literal 'radon-6.0.1' matches today and keeps matching until an actual upgrade, so nothing would catch it in the meantime. Force the same dynamism proof tree_git_sha already gets. Re-run the script in a subprocess whose PYTHONPATH carries a sitecustomize.py that patches importlib.metadata.version to return a sentinel string for the 'radon' distribution, and assert the report echoes that sentinel. A script reading the version at run time passes; a literal fails. This closes the gap that formula_version was otherwise the one provenance field verified only by coincidence.

criteria.statement: Two consecutive runs with different arguments, executed from one single working directory, leave the first run's own report readable and unchanged.
criteria.verification: From one directory, snapshot the full directory listing with per-file sha256 BEFORE the first run -- an independent snapshot taken by the test, not a list the tool reports about itself. Run token_bloat_diagnostic.py --project-hint dev-harness --days 30. Snapshot again: the diff of the two snapshots is the true set of files the run created or modified, whether or not the tool disclosed them. Then, from that same directory with no cd, run token_bloat_diagnostic.py --days 30 with no --project-hint. Every file in that true created set must still exist, still parse as JSON where it parsed before, still hash to its recorded sha256, and still carry project_hint == 'dev-harness'. Both a run-scoped-filename fix and a refuse-to-overwrite fix satisfy this. Overwriting in place fails; writing a run-scoped file while clobbering a fixed-name copy fails; and clobbering an undisclosed legacy companion file the tool never reports about itself also fails, which a self-reported path list would have missed.

criteria.statement: The non-clobbering behaviour generalizes across scopes rather than being keyed to this project's own recovery narrative: it holds for a project hint other than 'dev-harness', and for a sequence whose FIRST run carries no hint at all.
criteria.verification: Repeat C3's independent-snapshot procedure twice more from a single directory each time, with no cd between runs in a pair. Pair one: first run --project-hint tessera --days 30, second run --project-hint atlas --days 30; the tessera run's true created set must survive intact with project_hint == 'tessera'. Pair two, hint order inverted: first run --days 30 with NO --project-hint, second run --project-hint dev-harness --days 30; the unhinted run's true created set must survive intact with its own project_hint value. Neither pair mentions 'dev-harness' as the protected first run. An implementation that special-cases the literal string 'dev-harness', or that protects only hinted runs, passes C1 through C3 green and fails here. Pair three, and the reason it exists: the first two pairs name four concrete hint shapes, which a sufficiently bad-faith implementation could in principle hardcode as a set. So the third pair's protected run uses a hint string GENERATED AT TEST TIME (a random suffix, e.g. 'scopeprobe-' plus eight random hex characters), followed by a --project-hint dev-harness run; the generated-hint run's true created set must survive intact with its own hint echoed. A hint that matches no real project directory still produces a valid report with zero session files, which is a sufficient artifact for a persistence assertion. Because the value cannot be known before the test runs, no implementation can enumerate the set this criterion checks, which closes the class rather than adding a fifth fixed value to it.

criteria.statement: When git churn is degenerate -- every currently-analyzed file shares one churn value -- foreman_quality_baseline.py emits hotspot_signal_complexity_only instead of hotspot_signal for every entry (per_file_detail and hotspots_top15), sets meta.hotspot_signal_degenerate_churn to true, and writes a meta.hotspot_signal_note explaining why. Never silently as hotspot_signal, which would describe a single-input number as complexity x churn.
criteria.verification: Construct an isolated temp git repository whose Python files all carry the same real per-file commit count (e.g. one initial commit adding all of them, none touched again), run build_report() against it, and assert: meta['hotspot_signal_degenerate_churn'] is True; every per_file_detail entry and every hotspots_top15 entry carries 'hotspot_signal_complexity_only' and NOT 'hotspot_signal'; meta['hotspot_signal_note'] is a non-empty string naming the constant churn value. Degeneracy is detected from the real distribution (len(set(churn_values)) <= 1), not hardcoded to churn==1, so the criterion holds regardless of what the constant value is.

criteria.statement: When git churn is NOT degenerate, behavior is unchanged from before this fix: every entry carries hotspot_signal (the complexity x churn product), meta.hotspot_signal_degenerate_churn is false, no hotspot_signal_note is written, and hotspots_top15 ranks by the same product as before.
criteria.verification: Construct an isolated temp git repository with at least two Python files whose real per-file commit counts differ (e.g. one committed once, one edited and committed three times), run build_report() against it, and assert meta['hotspot_signal_degenerate_churn'] is False, every entry carries 'hotspot_signal' and not 'hotspot_signal_complexity_only', and the numeric hotspot_signal values equal max_cc * git_commits_touching_file for each file -- the exact pre-fix formula, proving the fix is additive (a new branch) rather than a rewrite of the existing behavior.

criteria.statement: security_privacy_convergence.py's cross_reference_code_findings(), the one real downstream consumer of foreman_quality_baseline.py's hotspots_top15 (R1's file-selection ranking), reads whichever signal key the quality report actually emitted (hotspot_signal or hotspot_signal_complexity_only) rather than assuming hotspot_signal unconditionally -- a KeyError or a silently-missing quality_compound row on the degenerate path is the exact regression this criterion exists to block. This repo's real per-file churn happened to be degenerate when DEVH-19 was filed but is not degenerate as of this freeze (this session's own commits since have spread it 1-4) -- the fix must not assume either state, since a squashed-history repo can revert to degenerate on its own at any time and this consumer must survive both.
criteria.verification: python3 -m unittest against a new test asserting cross_reference_code_findings() populates quality_compound with the correct quality_hotspot_signal value from both a degenerate-churn quality_report fixture (hotspot_signal_complexity_only present, hotspot_signal absent) and a non-degenerate one (hotspot_signal present) -- both must produce a populated, correctly-valued quality_compound row, not a KeyError and not a silently-empty one.

failure_criteria.statement: The three scripts are copied in and committed, provenance fields are added, and the reports still write to one fixed filename. C1 and C2 both go green, git history looks complete, and the tool goes on destroying prior evidence exactly as it did to the only dev-harness-scoped run anyone can point at.
failure_criteria.detection: C3 runs two invocations from a single directory and re-reads the first run's recorded paths by sha256. Passing C1 and C2 alone is not done.

failure_criteria.statement: Provenance keys are present but carry a literal, a stale cached value, or the string 'unknown'. A schema check that only tests key presence passes, and a report can no longer be traced to the code that produced it, which is the entire point of R23a.
failure_criteria.detection: C2 compares both SHAs against values the test computes itself from git, then forces a change and requires tree_git_sha to move.

failure_criteria.statement: Truncated, stubbed, or import-broken copies are committed. git ls-files returns all three paths and the requirement looks satisfied, but no report can actually be regenerated, so R3's before/after comparison is no more reproducible than it was before.
failure_criteria.detection: C1 requires each script to execute to exit 0 from a fresh directory and emit a parseable report, not merely to be tracked.

failure_criteria.statement: The fix is documented rather than enforced: a README line or a docstring tells the operator to run each invocation from a separate directory. Every criterion phrased around correct usage passes, and the next person who runs two scopes from one directory loses the first result again.
failure_criteria.detection: C3 deliberately runs both invocations from ONE directory with no cd between them. A convention that lives only in prose cannot pass it.

failure_criteria.statement: Provenance is backfilled onto the report files already sitting in /Users/m5/dev/dev-harness, making historical reports look traceable when the tool state that produced them was never recorded. This would manufacture exactly the false confidence PRD.md section 0.1 exists to warn about.
failure_criteria.detection: Backfilling historical reports is named in out_of_scope. C2 verifies provenance only on reports generated by a run the test itself performs.

failure_criteria.statement: The fix is keyed to the literal project hint 'dev-harness' -- an if project_hint == 'dev-harness' special case, or protection that applies only when the first run carries a hint at all. C1 through C3 go green because every one of them uses dev-harness as the protected first run, the PRD's own recovery narrative looks closed, and any two scoped runs from one directory can still destroy each other's evidence for every other project on the machine.
failure_criteria.detection: C4 runs two further pairs, neither using dev-harness as the protected run, one of them starting with no hint at all.

failure_criteria.statement: A script's per-file analysis silently breaks while the script still exits 0 and writes a well-formed report, for example {'files_analyzed': 0}. A criterion asking only for a non-empty top-level object passes, and R3's before/after comparison is run against a report that measured nothing.
failure_criteria.detection: C1 asserts content a working analysis must produce and a broken one cannot: file and function floors, and store.py present in the hotspots with its known max_cc and MI.

failure_criteria.statement: formula_version is a hardcoded literal. It is present and non-empty, so a presence check passes, and it goes on passing unchanged after a radon upgrade silently moves every maintainability number in every report -- the exact drift the field was added to make visible.
failure_criteria.detection: C2 compares the reported radon version against importlib.metadata.version('radon') queried by the test itself.

failure_criteria.statement: The disclosed output file is protected while an undisclosed companion file the tool never reports about itself is still clobbered. A verification built on the tool's own self-reported list of what it wrote cannot see this, because the tool defines the evidence used to judge it.
failure_criteria.detection: C3 and C4 both take an independent before/after directory snapshot with per-file sha256 and diff them, so the true created set is established by the test rather than reported by the subject.

failure_criteria.statement: formula_version is a literal that happens to equal the installed radon version, so every live-match check passes by coincidence and goes on passing until an upgrade -- the one event the field exists to surface. Distinct from F8: F8's detection was the live-match check itself, which this vector defeats.
failure_criteria.detection: C2's forced-dynamism step runs the script under a patched importlib.metadata.version and requires the sentinel to appear in the report.

failure_criteria.statement: The non-clobbering fix is keyed to the specific set of hint values the criteria name rather than to one literal string. Every enumerable pair passes and a fifth real hint still clobbers.
failure_criteria.detection: C4's third pair uses a hint generated at test time, so the checked set cannot be enumerated in advance.

failure_criteria.statement: The relabelling is hardcoded to trigger only when every churn value equals literally 1, rather than detected from the real distribution. A future commit that touches every analyzed file exactly twice (still degenerate, still single-signal) would silently re-emit the misleading hotspot_signal name.
failure_criteria.detection: C5's verification requires degeneracy to be computed as len(set(churn_values)) <= 1, not a churn==1 special case, and C6 proves the non-degenerate branch is a genuinely separate path rather than the same code with a hardcoded threshold.

failure_criteria.statement: The field is renamed on the degenerate path but security_privacy_convergence.py's cross_reference_code_findings() still does sources['quality_hotspot']['hotspot_signal'] unconditionally -- a KeyError on the very next real run against this repo, since this repo's own churn is degenerate today, or a swallowed exception that silently drops every quality_compound row.
failure_criteria.detection: C7 requires a test proving the consumer populates quality_compound correctly from BOTH a degenerate and a non-degenerate quality_report fixture.

out_of_scope: The correctness of any number these scripts produce. DEVH-4 (UTC day bucketing) and DEVH-5 (day-over-day ratio against an in-progress today) are open bugs in token_bloat_diagnostic.py and are separate tickets. R23 is provenance and persistence only.

Changing any metric formula other than the R18 hotspot-signal relabelling itself (C5-C7). A broader formula change under this freeze would invalidate the 6.86 baseline that R3's before/after comparison is measured against.
Backfilling provenance onto reports already generated. The tool state that produced them was not recorded and cannot be honestly reconstructed.
R21's KPI retention path under monitoring/quality-history/. Separate requirement, and blocked on DEVH-4 and DEVH-5 closing per concept-gate condition C3.
Committing report outputs to git. R23 makes a report reproducible; it does not make every run an archived artifact.
constraints: The three scripts do not exist in this worktree. They exist only in /Users/m5/dev/dev-harness and are untracked there. Untracked files are worktree-local and a shared .git directory does not carry them across, so git add alone cannot satisfy C1 -- the files must be copied into this tree first.

Copy the files as they are. Do not refactor, reformat, or fix DEVH-4 or DEVH-5 in the same change; a copy that also edits behaviour makes the committed baseline something other than the code that produced the existing reports. Exception, per the DEVH-19 amendment: C5-C7's hotspot-signal relabelling is the one deliberate behavior change this freeze now covers.

formula_version must be a real version string covering the radon version used for the maintainability index and an explicit tag for the hotspot formula, so that a dependency bump changing every number in a report is visible without a tool SHA change or a tree diff.
Provenance is computed at run time from the repository the script is analyzing, not read from a config file or an environment variable that a caller could set.

This file sits at the repository root because component_root('root-docs-and-scratch') resolves to the project root -- its first declared glob is a bare filename, so the empty prefix is correct. Criteria here originally covered R23 only; the DEVH-19 amendment (C5-C7) extends coverage specifically to the R18 hotspot-signal relabelling. Still do not land any OTHER root-level work under this freeze.

amendments.from: Asserted that a --project-hint dev-harness run survives a subsequent broader run -- the same protected hint C3 already uses, so C4 could not fail unless C3 also failed, and neither criterion ever tested another scope.
amendments.to: Rewritten as the generalization criterion: two further pairs, one using tessera then atlas, one starting with no hint at all, neither using dev-harness as the protected run.
amendments.reason: dev-harness-32 blind falsification pass. Arrived cold, with no prior briefing, and found four gaming vectors that would pass the original criteria all green. This finding subsumes a separate concern the criteria author had already self-reported to the orchestrator (that C4 could not fail independently of C3, and was therefore padding against scope_estimate.test_criteria). That self-report was deliberately withheld from the falsification pass to keep it blind; the pass arrived cold and found the sharper version of the same weakness unaided. One rewrite closes both: C4 now fails independently AND closes the special-casing vector.
